title: Germany and France push trade weapon to deny access to China
article:
(Oct 6): Germany and France are urging the European Union (EU) to adopt new powers that would enable the bloc to cut off access to its single market if China or other nations destabilise trade relations.

The suggestion came in a letter, seen by Bloomberg News, sent Monday to European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen, the top EU executive.

“We need a credible instrument in the hands of the Commission to allow for decisive and systemic reaction,” the letter reads, suggesting “powerful measures up to an immediate cut-off from the internal market if needed.”

The letter also calls for an instrument that would force Europe to reduce various supply chain dependencies on foreign countries.

While the letter does not specifically mention China, the EU is currently exploring ways to rebalance its trade relationship with the country. Having Germany and France aligned behind these proposals will give them significant heft going into an EU summit next week, where leaders will discuss the issue.

See also: Germany, France press EU to protect exporters from CO₂ rules

Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the proposal was devised in Berlin and Paris as the bloc is being “massively affected” by unfair trade practices — and the commission needs better tools.

“We want to enable the European Commission to act quickly when necessary,” Merz told reporters in Berlin. “The drawback of European trade policy in recent years has always been that decision-making took too long.”

German officials, speaking anonymously in line with government protocol, said the market-access tool should be seen as a second strike weapon in an all-out trade war with a country like China. It could be deployed, for instance, if China blocked all exports of rare earth materials, which the EU relies on to build modern technologies.

“The European Union is faced with unprecedented challenges,” the Franco-German letter says, arguing that countries are weaponising trade and distorting markets. “We need urgent action to address these threats, to diversify and to derisk.”

In addition to the new tools, Germany and France are urging the EU to more aggressively investigate whether entire sectors, such as chemicals, plastics and hybrid cars, are facing unfair competition from heavily subsidised imports. Such investigations could result in new tariffs.

Currently, such EU investigations tend to focus on specific products, not entire sectors.

EU leaders directed the commission in June to reengage with Beijing over the bloc’s trade deficit with China, which reached €360.6 billion last year and continued to widen in the first half of 2026.

In response, EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic launched a new series of talks with Beijing. He will travel to China at the end of the week to get a sense of where things stand ahead of the upcoming summit.

In parallel, EU policymakers in Brussels are also exploring possible new trade measures to let the EU react more swiftly and with greater force to countries undermining trade relationships. They are also looking at measures to encourage supply chain diversification.

title: US stocks get tech lift despite renewed bond losses
article:
(Oct 6): A rally in giant technology companies drove stocks higher, overshadowing concerns about still-elevated oil prices and bond yields.

The S&P 500 edged closer to a record as a gauge of megacaps climbed 1.2%. Renewed political uncertainty in Europe sent the euro to its weakest level since May 2025, driving Treasury yields up and boosting the dollar’s haven appeal. Brazilian assets soared as market-friendly Flávio Bolsonaro became the front-runner to win the presidential election runoff.

Bond yields are continuing their relentless march higher, but equities have been remarkably resilient — even though breadth beneath the surface has been historically weak, according to Jason Pride and Michael Reynolds at Glenmede.

With stocks near all-time highs, managing concentration risk and strengthening portfolio resilience remain important as investors navigate geopolitical risks and elevated bond yields, said Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi at UBS Chief Investment Office.

“We believe equities have room to move higher over the next six to 12 months amid resilient economic growth and robust earnings,” she noted. “But the path is unlikely to be smooth.”

See also: Qualcomm licenses patents on Huawei’s LogicFolding chip tech — Bloomberg

On the economic front, the US service sector expanded at a slower pace in September while a price gauge climbed to a four-year high. Overall, the data points to mounting inflationary pressures and strong nominal growth — reinforcing a central bond-bearish underpinning over the past several weeks, according to Vail Hartman at BMO Capital Markets.

The Treasury selloff that sent yields to multi-decade highs reflects stronger US growth and competition for capital rather than rising inflation concerns, according to Citadel Securities’ Nohshad Shah.

See also: US stocks advance after cooler-than-expected employment data

“Relative equity market calm amid the bond market’s ‘perfect storm’ is understandable, given accelerating economic growth and the AI boom’s rate insensitivity,” said Lisa Shalett at Morgan Stanley Wealth Management.

Investors have gotten too bearish on stocks, with earnings expected to remain robust and the surge in bond yields looking increasingly stretched, according to JPMorgan Chase & Co’s strategists led by Mislav Matejka.

A drop in US stock valuations has left some areas looking attractive as earnings growth shows few signs of waning, according to Morgan Stanley’s Michael Wilson. The extent of the pullback has created a “better setup” for sectors linked to the economic cycle where the fundamental outlook remains robust, he said.
• Intel Corp fell after a report on discussions of a potential collaboration between Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co and Elon Musk’s Terafab initiative, which the US chipmaker joined in April.
• Cerebras Systems Inc rallied after OpenAI chief executive officer Sam Altman said the company is a “close partner,” and the two firms have a deep engagement pushing on the frontiers of speed.
• CH Robinson Worldwide Inc agreed to buy trucking brokerage firm RXO Inc in a deal centered around a bet that artificial intelligence can help the companies improve efficiency in a challenging freight market.
• Cenovus Energy Inc agreed to buy Athabasca Oil Corp for about C$5.8 billion, expanding its footprint in the Canadian oil sands.
• Nvidia Corp partner Hon Hai Precision Industry Co reported better-than-expected quarterly revenue, signaling sustained and elevated spending on global AI infrastructure.

Pan Pacific Hotels to roll out 10 new-build and renovation projects across Southeast Asia in 2027
article:
Pan Pacific Hotels Group (PPHG) is accelerating investment in Southeast Asia. The UOL Group subsidiary has 10 new-build or major renovation projects planned across the region in 2027 as part of its ongoing portfolio transformation.

New properties comprise Pan Pacific Phnom Penh; Parkroyal Siem Reap; Siam Pan Pacific Bangkok; Pan Pacific Serviced Suites Thonglor, Bangkok; Parkroyal Hanoi; Parkroyal Serviced Suites Manila Bay and Parkroyal Jakarta.

Properties that will be renovated are Parkroyal Serviced Suites Kuala Lumpur; Parkroyal Gurney Bay Penang and Parkroyal Collection Pickering, Singapore.

The projects are part of PPHG’s “Version 2.0” strategy, which aims to change “not only how PPHG’s hotels look, but how they operate and engage with guests”, the group said in a release.

The strategy brings together internationally recognised architects and designers, biophilic and wellbeing-led design, enhanced sustainability infrastructure and technology-enabled experiences in a “comprehensive transformation” of PPHG’s portfolio.

Over half of the portfolio has undergone the programme since 2020, including newly built, redesigned or significantly renovated properties. Among these are the 237-room Pan Pacific London, which opened in 2021 and Pan Pacific Orchard, Singapore, which debuted in 2023.

The transformation comes amid an evolving hospitality landscape, with the boundaries between work, leisure, wellbeing and personal time becoming “increasingly fluid”, PPHG observed.

“The market has moved, and we have to move with it,” said Choe Peng Sum, CEO of PPHG.  “People are living differently, and therefore they are travelling differently.”

Against this backdrop, PPHG aims to make each brand under its portfolio “more distinctive and more relevant to the market it serves”. “Our ambition is to have a portfolio where each brand has a clear reason to exist, but where the group as a whole has the operating breadth to capture different forms of demand,” Choe explained.

PHG owns and manages over 50 hotels, resorts and serviced suites across three brands: the luxury offering Pan Pacific, the upscale proposition Parkroyal, and Parkroyal Collection, which comprises hotels positioned around nature, sustainability and wellbeing.

title: Marriott inks deal for two properties in Thailand's Khao Lak
article:
Marriott International has signed an agreement with Thailand’s KS Hotels & Resorts to manage two properties in Khao Lak, Thailand. The properties are located on Matalay, a new 200ha resort destination KS Hotels is developing in the area.

Located about 75 minutes away by car from Phuket International Airport, Matalay will include hotels, residences, a conference centre, an elephant sanctuary, community facilities, and green spaces.

The two properties under Marriott — Moxy Khao Lak Memories Beach and Matalay Khao Lak, Apartments by Marriott Bonvoy — are situated at Matalay’s northern end. They are close to Memories Beach, a known surf spot.

The 160-key Moxy hotel will be the first in Southern Thailand. It will include a pool, a restaurant and bar, a gym and a beachfront events lawn.

Matalay Khao Lak, Apartments by Marriott Bonvoy will offer 60 two-bedroom apartments for longer stays. Each apartment will come with a full kitchen and a washer-dryer. This will mark the serviced apartment brand’s Thai debut.

Marriott already operates JW Marriott Khao Lak Resort & Spa, located just south of Matalay. The hotel, which opened in 2009, shares the same beachfront as the upcoming properties and will also be connected through a new 3km jogging and cycling track.

title: South Korea’s Shinhan Card completes sale of Seoul office building for KRW800 bil
article:
Shinhan Card has completed the sale of Pine Avenue Tower A, a prime office building in Seoul, South Korea, for KRW800 billion (around $762 million).

Colliers advised on the deal. In an Oct 5 release, it called the sale "one of the largest transactions of its kind in 2026."

The South Korean credit card company divested the building, which serves as its headquarters, to MDM Asset Management through a sale-and-leaseback arrangement. MDM Asset Management is an investment firm under MDM Group, a South Korean real estate and finance conglomerate.

Shinhan Card had acquired Pine Avenue Tower A for KRW521.5 billion in 2020 from the State Oil Fund of the Republic of Azerbaijan.

The company will continue using the building as its headquarters through a 10-year lease.

“Despite a highly selective investment landscape driven by rising interest rates, we successfully unlocked the true value of Pine Avenue Tower A by structuring a stable, long-term sale-and-leaseback that appealed directly to core investors,” said Sungwook Cho, Colliers’ managing director and head of capital markets and investment services for Korea.

Colliers has helped broker several office asset sales in Korea this year, including Eulji Twin Tower, Hana Insurance Building and Gangnam 358 Tower.

The sale of Pine Avenue Tower A brings the combined value of office deals the firm has advised on to KRW 3.42 trillion, according to the firm.

title: Freehold residential site at Joo Chiat Terrace up for sale at $17.5 mil
article:
A freehold residential site at 146 and 148 Joo Chiat Terrace has been launched for collective sale at $17.5 million.

A three-storey residential block currently occupies the plot. Built in 1987, it comprises six apartments.

Owners of all six homes have consented to the en bloc sale, according to AlpsEdge Real Estate and Brilliance Capital, which are jointly marketing the property. The unanimous consent means the sale can avoid "the prolonged statutory process" for obtaining the relevant approvals for the collective sale, the firms added in an Oct 5 release.

The site spans a land area of about 10,247 sq ft zoned for residential use, with a gross plot ratio of 1.4.

At $17.5 million, the site’s price works out to around $1,220 psf per plot ratio (psf ppr). The figure is in line with recent comparable transactions, which were done at land rates ranging from $1,110 to $1,175 psf ppr, the joint marketing agents said.

These include the sale of a freehold detached home at 108 Joo Chiat Terrace for $21.5 million ($1,175 psf ppr) in December 2024 and a trio of freehold terraced homes on Tanjong Katong Road plot that transacted for $10.86 million ($1,110 psf ppr) in March 2025.

Another recent comparable is Chiku Mansions , a four-storey walk-up block on Chiku Road that Macly Group bought for roughly $22 million ($1,168 psf ppr) in September last year. Macly is expected to redevelop the freehold site into a new boutique residential project with fewer than 20 units.

Meanwhile, the site at 108 Joo Chiat Terrace is now Verdé Joo Chiat, an 18-unit, five-storey residential block currently under construction. Caveats lodged show nine units have been sold since it launched in May, fetching prices from $2,278 to $2,484 psf.

The response points to “encouraging take-up for small, low-rise boutique projects” in the Joo Chiat and Katong precincts, said Carin Puah, executive director at AlpsEdge.

Other recent launches in the vicinity include Straits at Joo Chiat , a 16-unit freehold development on Joo Chiat Place, and Koon Seng House , a 17-unit apartment on Koon Seng Road. Both projects launched in 2024 and are fully sold. Units at the developments fetched prices ranging from around $2,000 to $2,350 psf.

The success of the launches provides “encouraging market validation” for the future development at 146 and 148 Joo Chiat Terrace, added Puah.

The site is located within the established Joo Chiat and Katong residential, heritage and lifestyle enclaves, with amenities such as I12 Katong, Parkway Parade and East Coast Park a five- to 10-minute drive away.

Tanjong Katong Primary School and Haig Girls’ School are within 1 km of the site.  It is also within approximately 2km of other schools, such as Tao Nan School, CHIJ (Katong) Primary and Ngee Ann Primary.

The tender for 146 and 148 Joo Chiat Terrace will close at 3pm on Nov 17.

title: SGX Board Lot Reduction: 8 Stocks Set to Benefit in October 2026
article:
Today, you will need far less money to buy into some of Singapore’s
blue chips
.
As of 5 October 2026, the Singapore Exchange (SGX) has cut the standard board lot size for 11 securities from 100 shares down to 10.
A S$32 stock that used to require S$3,200 per lot will now require just S$320 to get started.
The change covers securities that trade above S$10 or US$10 for US dollar counters.
The shares you already own stay as they are, and SGX will review eligible stocks every quarter.
Once a lot shrinks, it stays small.
Do note that SGX cleared all resting orders for these counters at the close of trading on Friday, 2 October.
You will need to re-enter any unfilled orders today.
A cheaper ticket makes these companies easier to own, but it does nothing to alter the fundamental quality of the underlying businesses.
Following our earlier look at
four featured stocks from the first batch
, this second instalment examines another four counters set to benefit from the lower trading threshold.
How did OCBC grow profit while its margin shrank?
Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation Limited
(SGX: O39), or OCBC, Singapore’s longest-established bank, earned less on each dollar it lent in 1H2026.
Its net interest margin (NIM) narrowed by 0.25 percentage points to 1.73%.
The bank partly offset the margin compression by expanding its loan book.
Customer loans grew 12% year on year (YoY) to S$364.5 billion, which limited the drop in net interest income (NII) to just 3%, bringing it to S$4.5 billion.
Non-interest income filled the gap and then some, climbing 36% to S$3.5 billion as trading income rose 46% and insurance income surged 49%.
Consequently, total income rose 11% to S$8.0 billion, while the non-performing loan (NPL) ratio remained stable at 0.9%.
Net profit rose 13% to a record S$4.2 billion, prompting the board to lift the interim dividend by 15% to S$0.47 per share.
Management upgraded its FY2026 guidance on 7 August and now expects only a slight dip in full-year net interest income.

What drove UOB’s profit growth?
United Overseas Bank Limited
(SGX: U11), or UOB, which serves more than 8 million retail customers across ASEAN, felt a similar squeeze.
As benchmark rates fell, its NIM narrowed from 1.96% to 1.78%, while NII eased 3% YoY to S$4.6 billion.
Wealth management fees rose 15%, though loan-related fees fell 19%.
Total income slipped 1% to S$7.0 billion and operating profit before allowances declined 4% to S$3.9 billion.
Despite these headwinds, net profit still rose 3% to S$2.9 billion.
UOB achieved this by setting aside less money for bad loans, as total allowances fell 27% to S$414 million.
One-off asset sale gains also boosted other income, while the non-performing loan ratio held steady at 1.6%.
UOB paid an interim dividend of S$0.88 per share on 28 August, up from S$0.85 per share a year ago.

Hongkong Land, DFI Retail and lower financing costs drove the gains.

title: 3 Singapore Stocks That Have Raised Their Dividends for 5 Years or More

Companies that consistently raise their dividends are demonstrating something real: growing earnings, cash generation, and more importantly, a willingness to share more of it with shareholders.
But a growth streak proves nothing about the future.
Three companies stand out for raising their dividends steadily over the past five years.

A few things separate a genuine dividend grower from a company that just happens to pay more this year.
Earnings need to be rising, giving the business room to pay out more without straining itself.
The earnings growth should also show up in cash, not just on paper — a company can report a healthy profit and still struggle to pay a dividend if the cash isn’t there.
The payout ratio matters too: pay out too little, and shareholders miss out; pay out too much, and there’s nothing left to reinvest.
And debt should stay manageable, since a business weighed down by loans has far less room to keep paying a dividend when conditions turn tough.
It’s a bonus if the business has an edge, such as a regulatory moat, that helps keep growth humming through different business cycles.
DBS Group Holdings (SGX: D05) – The Blue-Chip Dividend Grower
This financial powerhouse has seen its dividend nearly triple since 2021 – from S$1.09 per share to S$3.06 in 2025 (including S$0.60 of capital return dividends), which represents a 29% compound annual growth rate (CAGR).
Moreover, the dividend has been on a mostly consistent upward path, with only 2023’s dividend dipping compared to the prior year due to a one-off special dividend in 2022.
It’s not hard to see why DBS’s dividend growth has been so robust.
In the latest quarter ended 30 June 2026 (2Q2026), DBS posted record total income and net profit of S$6.1 billion and S$3.1 billion, respectively.
The former grew 6% year on year (YoY) while the latter was up 9% and supported a strong return on equity (ROE) of 17.9%.
There is room for further dividend increases.
DBS pays out only around 60% of its profit as ordinary dividends, leaving the rest of its profit for reinvestment.
Meanwhile, its fully phased-in Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio of 14.6% gives it a solid buffer to keep paying through tough times.
Finally, a booming wealth management business supports further dividend growth.

Singapore Exchange Limited (SGX: S68), or SGX – The Defensive Dividend Compounder
SGX’s total dividend rose from S$0.32 per share in FY2021 (financial year ended 30 June 2021) to S$0.57 per share in FY2026, including a one-off additional dividend of S$0.125 from capital recycling gains.
This translated to a 12.2% CAGR over five years, although the dividend record includes one flat year in FY2022.
As a toll-booth business that effectively earns fees on trading and clearing across equities, derivatives, currencies and commodities, SGX’s earnings and free cash flow (FCF) hold up even during weaker economic periods.
This is best seen in its historical dividend payments, which have held even during weaker markets.
Further dividend growth comes down to SGX’s ability to maintain its steady revenue growth over the years and a historically disciplined payout ratio (around 60% to 80% of earnings).
The bourse operator’s solid balance sheet with minimal net debt further fortifies its future dividend payments.

Singapore Technologies Engineering Ltd (SGX: S63), or STE – The Higher-Growth Dividend Payer
The last name on this list may not have consistently increased its dividends year after year, but its five-year track record is nothing to scoff at.
STE’s total dividend rose from S$0.15 per share in 2021 to S$0.23 in 2025 (including a S$0.05 special dividend) – an 11.3% CAGR.
Although the starting and current yields are low, STE’s dividend growth has been backed by a record order book (S$35.7 billion as of 30 June 2026), strong free cash flow generation, and strong demand in its key aerospace and defence markets.
As long as the company keeps winning orders and does a solid job of converting its order book into earnings and cash flow, it is likely that STE keep raising its dividends.
This is reinforced by a dividend policy, announced in March 2025, to pay about one-third of each year’s increase in net profit as additional dividends.
Related articles:
DBS, Singtel and ST Engineering Have Rallied: Which Is Still Worth Buying?

Why Dividend Growth Can Matter More Than a High Starting Yield
A simple illustration: Stock A yields 6% today but never raises its payout, while Stock B starts at 3.5% but grows its dividend 7% a year.
On a S$10,000 stake, Stock A pays S$600 a year, indefinitely. Stock B starts at S$350, but because it grows 7% a year, its annual payout overtakes Stock A’s after about eight years of increases, and keeps pulling ahead after that.
This is yield on cost: your income measured against your original
investment, not today’s price. A dividend that keeps growing can turn a modest starting yield into a substantial one over a long enough horizon – something a static high yield can never do.
What Should Investors Watch Out For?
Monitor
quarterly earnings and whether they translate into real free cash flow.
Key red flags include weakening cash flows, a payout ratio stretching beyond earnings, rising debt used to fund dividends, or sudden high capital expenditure requirements.
The best dividend growers are simply businesses whose earnings and cash flow keep growing faster than what they pay out – not businesses stretching to pay more than they earn.
Get Smart: Look for Dividends That Can Keep Growing
DBS, SGX and STE have all
raised their dividends
over the past five years, but not one of them did it every single year — each had a flat or uneven stretch somewhere along the way.
That’s worth remembering before crediting any company with a clean streak.
The dividend itself is really just the output – what decides whether it keeps rising is the business behind it.
Check the earnings, cash flow, payout ratio and debt behind it, and the yield on the label matters a lot less.
Over a long horizon, a steadily rising dividend – even an imperfect one – can become a genuinely powerful source of compounding income.

.
What changes on 5 October?
A
board lot
is the smallest number of shares you can trade in one go on the Singapore Exchange (SGX).
For most counters today, that number is 100.
Under the new rules, eligible stocks priced above S$10 and up to S$100 will trade in lots of 10.

If you already hold these shares, your existing holdings remain unchanged.
However, keep in mind that SGX will purge all resting orders for these counters at the close of the final trading day before 5 October, so you will need to re-enter them.
Can SGX keep raising its dividend?
Singapore Exchange Limited
(SGX: S68) runs Singapore’s stock market and a multi-asset exchange, and it also happens to be on its own list of first-batch counters.
For the financial year ended 30 June 2026 (FY2026), net revenue grew 13.9% year on year (YoY) to S$1.5 billion.
Equities–Cash revenue led the charge, rising 28.1% to S$502.9 million as securities daily average traded value expanded by 34.9%.
A S$53.4 million goodwill impairment held net profit growth to 7.8%, bringing the total to S$698.4 million.
Strip that out, along with weaker investment gains, and adjusted net profit rose 24.6% to S$759.5 million.
SGX clearly maintains the cash flow required to support its payouts.
It generated S$870.7 million in operating cash flow while holding S$1.8 billion in cash against S$628.2 million in borrowings.
For FY2026, the ordinary dividend came to S$0.445 per share, complemented by a one-off dividend of S$0.125 per share.
Looking ahead, management has guided for quarterly dividend increases of 0.25 cents through FY2028.
How is DBS growing as rates fall?
DBS Group Holdings Ltd
(SGX: D05), Singapore’s largest lender, has had to navigate falling interest rates that are putting pressure on its lending margins.
In the second quarter of 2026 (2Q2026), the net interest margin narrowed by 18 basis points to 1.87%, leading to a 2% YoY dip in net interest income to S$3.6 billion.
Fortunately, wealth management more than offset the shortfall.
Wealth management fees jumped 42% to S$919 million, pushing total non-interest income up 21% to S$2.5 billion.
Total income grew 6% to S$6.1 billion – marking the first time DBS has crossed the S$6 billion threshold in a quarter.
Net profit rose 9% to S$3.1 billion, delivering a healthy return on equity (ROE) of 17.9%.
DBS
declared an ordinary interim dividend of S$0.66 per share alongside a capital return dividend of S$0.15 per share.
What supports Haw Par’s dividend?
Haw Par Corporation
(SGX: H02) derives most of its operational revenue from its iconic Tiger Balm brand, though the bulk of its underlying profit comes from substantial equity stakes in UOB and
UOL Group
(SGX: U14).
Both slowed in the first half of 2026 (1H2026).
Revenue fell 8.2% YoY to S$115.9 million as consumer sentiment softened, while dividend income from its investments dropped to S$73.2 million from S$102.3 million.
Consequently, net profit slid 25.2% to S$107.9 million.
Because free cash flow underpins dividend durability, investors should note that Haw Par’s thinned to S$20.8 million from S$26.3 million.
However, the balance sheet tells a reassuringly conservative story: Haw Par held S$669.1 million in cash and S$212.3 million in debt securities against just S$52.6 million in total borrowings.
Haw Par declared an interim dividend of S$0.20 per share, matching last year’s payout.
It did not declare a special dividend for FY2025, following a S$1.00 special dividend distributed for FY2024.
What should Keppel shareholders watch?
Keppel Ltd
(SGX: BN4) is a Singapore-headquartered global asset manager and operator.
In 1H2026, revenue grew 24.6% YoY to S$3.8 billion.
However, a S$375 million loss within its non-core portfolio dragged overall net profit down 59.0% to S$154.7 million.
Excluding that non-core drag, net profit actually rose 25% to S$530 million.
Cash flow is the weaker spot.
Operating cash flow dropped to S$96.8 million from S$219.4 million due to higher working capital requirements, placing greater emphasis on asset sales.
Keppel
has announced roughly S$1.7 billion in asset monetisation so far this year, against a full-year target of S$2 billion to S$3 billion.
It held S$2.2 billion in cash against S$11.3 billion in borrowings.
Keppel declared an interim dividend of S$0.15 per share, unchanged from a year ago.
Watch operating cash flow and the pace of asset sales.
Get Smart: Buy the business, not the lot size
Buying one lot of a S$32 stock used to require an upfront capital outlay of S$3,200.
Under the revised trading rules, S$320 is all you need to get started.
That said, a smaller entry price does not guarantee a safer dividend payout.
Before taking a position, ask yourself where next year’s dividend will come from, and look for clear answers within the latest financial results.
If the fundamental numbers hold up, a smaller lot size simply works in your favour.
If they do not, you have found a cheaper way into the same risk.

title: Germany and France push trade weapon to deny access to China
article:
(Oct 6): Germany and France are urging the European Union (EU) to adopt new powers that would enable the bloc to cut off access to its single market if China or other nations destabilise trade relations.

The suggestion came in a letter, seen by Bloomberg News, sent Monday to European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen, the top EU executive.

“We need a credible instrument in the hands of the Commission to allow for decisive and systemic reaction,” the letter reads, suggesting “powerful measures up to an immediate cut-off from the internal market if needed.”

The letter also calls for an instrument that would force Europe to reduce various supply chain dependencies on foreign countries.

While the letter does not specifically mention China, the EU is currently exploring ways to rebalance its trade relationship with the country. Having Germany and France aligned behind these proposals will give them significant heft going into an EU summit next week, where leaders will discuss the issue.

See also: Germany, France press EU to protect exporters from CO₂ rules

Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the proposal was devised in Berlin and Paris as the bloc is being “massively affected” by unfair trade practices — and the commission needs better tools.

“We want to enable the European Commission to act quickly when necessary,” Merz told reporters in Berlin. “The drawback of European trade policy in recent years has always been that decision-making took too long.”

German officials, speaking anonymously in line with government protocol, said the market-access tool should be seen as a second strike weapon in an all-out trade war with a country like China. It could be deployed, for instance, if China blocked all exports of rare earth materials, which the EU relies on to build modern technologies.

“The European Union is faced with unprecedented challenges,” the Franco-German letter says, arguing that countries are weaponising trade and distorting markets. “We need urgent action to address these threats, to diversify and to derisk.”

In addition to the new tools, Germany and France are urging the EU to more aggressively investigate whether entire sectors, such as chemicals, plastics and hybrid cars, are facing unfair competition from heavily subsidised imports. Such investigations could result in new tariffs.

Currently, such EU investigations tend to focus on specific products, not entire sectors.

EU leaders directed the commission in June to reengage with Beijing over the bloc’s trade deficit with China, which reached €360.6 billion last year and continued to widen in the first half of 2026.

In response, EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic launched a new series of talks with Beijing. He will travel to China at the end of the week to get a sense of where things stand ahead of the upcoming summit.

In parallel, EU policymakers in Brussels are also exploring possible new trade measures to let the EU react more swiftly and with greater force to countries undermining trade relationships. They are also looking at measures to encourage supply chain diversification.

title: Sugar extends rally to highest level since 2024 on weather risks
article:
(Oct 5): Raw sugar futures extended gains, with worries about tighter global supplies mounting because of weather and production concerns across top growers.

The most-active contract in New York rose as much as 2% to its highest level since Dec 17, 2024. Monday’s session built on last week’s gain of nearly 8%. White sugar also rose.

The El Niño weather pattern is stirring supply concerns across the agriculture complex, with sugar expected to be among the first crops affected. At the start of the year, a supply glut was widely forecast, but weather risks have flipped that narrative to expectations of a deficit.

“Weather concerns are driving the latest uptick in sugar prices, which are poised to test the August highs,” said Chris Beauchamp, the chief market analyst of investing and trading platform IG.

Excessive rainfall has slowed cane harvesting and crushing in top producer Brazil. In second-biggest producer India, the weakest monsoon since 2015 has reduced projected sugar output to about 30 million tons. In Europe, sugar-beet yields are forecast to be 11% below the five-year average, according to the European Union’s Monitoring Agricultural Resources unit.

See also: Copper gains as US jobs data offers relief on fed tightening

While weaker output in one region can typically be offset by stronger production elsewhere, adverse conditions across several key growers at the same time could erode that buffer.

“It seems the market is convinced that sugar will fall well short of early and recent estimates,” Green Pool Global analysts wrote in a note on Monday, cutting their Central-South Brazil 2026/27 sugar output forecast by 3%.

Money managers became more bullish on raw sugar as they unwound bearish bets, with outright short positions falling to their lowest in more than 21 months, according to CFTC data through Sept 29.

title: Germany, France press EU to protect exporters from CO₂ rules
article:
(Oct 5): France and Germany are leading a push to force the European Union to come up with a better way of protecting exporters against tightening rules on carbon dioxide emissions.

The countries will press the European Commission, the bloc’s executive branch, to propose a solution that will help prevent industries moving away from the region as it tightens climate rules, according to a draft document seen by Bloomberg News. The push is set to draw widespread support, including from other big economies like Spain and Italy.

Over the next decade, the EU is phasing out a system of free emissions allowances under its carbon market, meaning that heavy industries will have to pay for the CO₂ they release into the atmosphere. While the bloc is also implementing a so-called carbon border levy to ensure that imports are subject to the same costs, there are concerns that exports by European companies will be insufficiently protected.

“The gradual increase in carbon costs for EU producers, if left uncompensated, risks undermining EU competitiveness in third-country markets and may lead to carbon leakage,” the document says. “It therefore requires a European solution.”

The latest initiative comes as EU nations and the bloc’s parliament negotiate a reform of the Emissions Trading System put forward by the commission in July. Climate ministers are set to debate the planned changes at a meeting in Luxembourg on Oct 12, before leaders from the 27 member states meet in Brussels later in the week.

The EU has so far taken limited action. A temporary decarbonisation fund announced in December last year provides a partial stopgap solution over two years. Other potential measures have been dismissed due to concerns they would run foul of World Trade Organization rules.

Spokespeople from France and Germany didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: Global oil supply buffer running ‘scarily thin’, Aramco CEO says
article:
(Oct 5): The oil stockpiles that cushion the world from supply shocks have become “scarily thin”, putting markets at risk of worsening unless the Strait of Hormuz reopens, according to the head of Saudi Arabia’s state producer.

The head of the world’s single biggest crude exporting company was speaking just days after governments in the world’s biggest economies announced plans to release as much as 100 million barrels of emergency oil and diesel stocks to ease rising fuel costs.

“Until Hormuz fully reopens and confidence returns, the crude reality is that pressure at both ends of the barrel will intensify,” Amin Nasser, the chief executive of Saudi Aramco, said at the Energy Intelligence Forum in London on Monday. “While the squeeze on crude is serious, refined fuel prices have risen even more sharply.”

Consumption of crude is still rising and countries will require even more supply for at least the next two years while rebuilding their inventories, Nasser said. That could mean additional demand of at least two million barrels a day, or even more if governments decide to increase the amount of oil they hold in stockpiles, he said.

When the US-Iran war began, the world had about 10 billion barrels of oil stocks, Nasser said. That has fallen to less than six billion, about 10% of which is practically available due to various technical restrictions, he said.

Releasing part of what’s left in global stockpiles will buy economies some time but won’t fix the imbalances between supply and demand, Nasser said. Gulf producers are working to ramp up production and exports and have succeeded in boosting crude flows to near prewar levels.

See also: LNG trade through Hormuz extends rebound despite shipping risks

Saudi Arabia and neighbours like the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait have been using their own tankers to ship crude through Hormuz, which has been at least partly obstructed since the US and Israel attacked Iran at the end of February, kicking off a regional war.

The higher flows have provided scant relief for oil markets, which are still pricing in security risks to supply in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea. Brent crude, the international benchmark, has traded around US$100 ($128.04) a barrel over the past month, even as more tankers transited Hormuz. Those vessels have had to run the risk of heightened attacks, while Saudi Arabia has been repeatedly targeted over the last month.

Still, all of Aramco’s upstream capacity remains intact, Nasser said. That has allowed the company to continue covering its supply contracts with buyers in Europe and Asia. The company has used various export routes, shifted supply between its different crude grades and pressed its own tankers into operation to supply customers, he said.

See also: OPEC+ agrees to keep oil output targets steady in November

Over the past month, Aramco boosted crude shipments from its main export terminal at Ras Tanura in the Persian Gulf. The company reacted quickly to a temporary halt to its main cross-country pipeline after an attack last month, and has since brought flows back to about 80% of capacity.

Aramco is looking for alternative crude export routes to avoid relying too much on any single method of reaching global buyers, Nasser said, without providing specifics. The company is studying plans that would double or triple the capacity of its storage facilities, he said.

title: The only billionaires making money this year are in tech
article:
(Oct 5): If 2026 feels like a banner year for the world’s tech billionaires, the numbers bear it out.

The roughly 100 technology fortunes among the world’s 500 richest people gained a combined US$845 billion through Sept 30, the most ever for the first nine months of a year, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

Fuelling that surge were the same forces driving global markets: the artificial intelligence (AI) boom and soaring technology stocks, particularly in the US. Tech billionaires are now worth a combined US$4.6 trillion, accounting for 36% of the index’s wealth despite making up only about a fifth of its members.

The divergence is stark. Billionaires who made their fortunes outside technology lost a combined US$62 billion over the period, while Americans accounted for 94% of the index’s net gains. Since Sept 10, all 10 of the world’s richest people have been from the US — the first time that’s happened since Bloomberg began tracking billionaires in 2012.

The gains have also been heavily concentrated at the very top. Elon Musk, the world’s richest person, added US$310 billion to his fortune this year through the end of September, or roughly 40% of the index’s total increase. He briefly became the world’s first trillionaire after SpaceX merged with his AI company, xAI, and went public in June.

See also: US lead in AI over China narrows after DeepSeek gains, Bloomberg Intelligence says

Nine of the world’s 10 wealthiest people owe their fortunes to American tech firms. Dell Technologies Inc founder Michael Dell saw his wealth increase 81% to US$254 billion as his company’s data centre sales business ballooned. Mark Zuckerberg added US$23 billion to his net worth this year as shares of Meta Platforms Inc gained 27% in September — its best month in almost four years — after rolling out its new Muse personal AI assistant.

The world’s 500 richest people hit a peak of US$13.4 trillion in combined wealth in mid-June. That’s since fallen 6% to US$12.6 trillion amid a broader market slowdown and growing doubts about some of the biggest AI names.

See also: Ex-Anthropic researcher Coxon to testify at NYC hearing on AI

The historic debt binge fuelling Big Tech’s AI ambitions is making some investors uneasy. Larry Ellison briefly became the world’s richest person in September 2025, gaining US$89 billion in a single day after Oracle Corp touted explosive growth in its AI-linked cloud infrastructure business.

A year later, Ellison’s net worth has fallen US$196 billion, while Oracle’s credit-default swaps are trading near record highs as investors balk at the massive borrowing needed to fund its AI infrastructure buildout.

The surge in billionaire wealth has also fuelled calls for higher taxes on the ultra-rich. California voters will decide in November whether to levy a wealth tax on the state’s billionaires, while states including Washington, New York, Illinois and Rhode Island have also discussed new taxes on wealthy residents.

The increasingly young, tech-heavy ranks of the ultra-rich also complicate the idea that the next great wealth shift will come primarily from ageing baby boomers passing fortunes to their heirs.

“We talk a lot about the great wealth transfer — but for the top 100 or 1,000 richest, some may be old and own rather traditional businesses, but a lot of them are young tech entrepreneurs,” said James Mazeau, an economist at UBS Group AG’s chief investment office. “I wonder to what extent that will fuel more wealth concentration.”

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

While much of the AI boom’s wealth has accrued to the leaders of major tech firms, Bloomberg’s new entrants show how the surge is also minting fortunes among startup founders and the companies supplying AI infrastructure.

All seven of Anthropic PBC’s co-founders joined the wealth list in June after the AI firm closed a funding round valuing it at US$965 billion. Founders of Chinese firms including MiniMax Group Inc’s Yan Junjie and DeepSeek’s Liang Wenfeng also were added.

The boom has also enriched the businesses supplying AI’s hardware and infrastructure.

Lin Tsung-chi, founder of King Slide, a Taiwanese maker of server rails and cable management systems for data centres, emerged with a US$9.5 billion fortune this year, four decades after starting the company. Wang Xin, chair of Guangdong Dtech Technology Co, joined the wealth index as AI created demand for the specialised drill bits her company makes to assemble circuit boards.

Two heirs of Samsung Electronics Co’s Lee family — Boo-jin and Seo-hyun — also joined the list thanks to demand for the company’s memory chips. The uptick in Samsung’s stock price helped the family pay back an US$8 billion inheritance tax after former chairman Lee Kun-hee’s death in 2020. In Taiwan, chip designer MediaTek Inc’s Tsai Ming-kai and Morris Chang, founder of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, also joined the exclusive list this year.

China’s push for technology independence and rivalry with the US for AI dominance have resulted in several new entrants joining the list: Suzhou TFC Optical Communication Co’s Zou Zhinong and family, as well as Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing Co’s Yuan Fugen.

title: UK expected to follow EU with China EV tariffs, report says
article:
(Oct 5): The UK is preparing to impose import levies on Chinese electric vehicles to meet a key demand from the European Union, the Times of London reported, in a blow to a group that now accounts for nearly one in four cars sold in the country.

Brussels has made clear that the UK faces being cut from the Made in Europe local-content rules if it does not act on the tariffs, the newspaper said, adding that EU officials are concerned the UK could become a backdoor for Chinese exports into Europe.

UK Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said on the sidelines of the Labour Party conference in Liverpool last week that he was keeping the situation regarding tariffs on Chinese EVs “under review". A person familiar with the matter said that remained the government’s position.

“We have not put tariffs on Chinese EVs,” Britain’s Department for Business, Science, Innovation and Trade said in a statement. “We continue to engage closely with industry so that our approach reflects the sector’s and UK’s national interests.”

UK officials are concerned about Chinese retaliation against Jaguar Land Rover Automotive plc but have determined the potential economic fallout of being dropped from the Made in Europe mechanism would be far more damaging, the Times said, without stating how the information was obtained.

Mike Hawes, CEO of the Society of Motor Manufacturers & Traders, described the reports of trade restrictions as unconfirmed. “Any such consideration would need to be based on robust evidence, follow due process and reflect the interests of consumers, manufacturers, investors and exporters,” said Hawes, who added that the government’s priority should be avoiding the exclusion of UK-built vehicles from the Made in Europe plan.

See also: Burnham takes on pensions and Brexit in sweeping change agenda

London introducing import duties would be a setback to Chinese automakers. Brands including BYD Co, SAIC Motor Corp’s MG and Chery Automobile Co’s Jaecoo have expanded quickly in the UK, where they do not face the additional tariffs on EVs currently in place in the EU. They grabbed 23% of British new-car sales in September, with the Jaecoo 7 the country’s best-selling new model.

The sport utility vehicle, which starts at around £30,000, has been dubbed the “Temu Range Rover” on social media for being a cheaper version of the British luxury brand, in a nod to the Chinese discount marketplace.

In the EU, Chinese brands are instead expanding with hybrid vehicles that are not yet hit with levies. In many cases, their EVs remain competitive even after tariffs. Companies led by BYD are also setting up local production to sidestep the duties.

See also: Burnham says Britain could rejoin EU after next election

The European Commission, meanwhile, has proposed the local-content rules to defend its industry. The measures could restrict key subsidies to vehicles manufactured in the bloc and exclude the UK operations of automakers like Land Rover and Nissan Motor Co. To be given equal treatment, the UK may also have to slap tariffs on Chinese EV imports, a Nissan executive said last month.

China’s automakers likely will not be deterred from their export push by rising trade barriers as fierce price competition continues in their home market.

“Tariffs come and go but it won’t change our investment in the UK,” Victor Zhang, UK managing director of Jaecoo and Omoda, which is also owned by Chery, recently told reporters on a call. “We are here to stay.”

title: BT buys over TalkTalk to save UK's broadband provider from collapse
article:
(Oct 5): BT Group plc bought TalkTalk and PlatformX Communications Ltd out of administration, preventing the collapse of a UK broadband provider that is also a major customer.

 

The deal, which is expected to have a total cash impact of £400 million for the 2027 fiscal year, was made “in the public interest” after talks to sell TalkTalk’s consumer and wholesale businesses fell through, BT said in a statement on Monday.

“This is a genuinely unprecedented situation, where millions of citizens and businesses were at risk if TalkTalk had collapsed,” BT chief executive officer Allison Kirkby said in the statement. “Our immediate priority is to stabilise the business and provide a safety net for the households and businesses who rely on TalkTalk.”

TalkTalk has struggled under its debt load since it was bought out in 2021 by Toscafund Asset Management LLP and private equity firm Penta Capital. The company was founded as a low-cost broadband provider, reselling wholesale access on BT’s Openreach network to consumers. However, high levels of competition and persistent inflation undermined its business.

The deal will pay off after TalkTalk’s business stabilises and the companies combine operations, according to BT, which maintained its financial targets.

BT shares rose 1.5% to 199.2 pence at 8.56am in London.

TalkTalk ended talks with Octopus Investments to sell its wholesale network division, Sky News reported last month. That came after discussions with the private equity firm Epiris didn’t result in a deal.

See also: Keppel and StarHub in ‘ongoing discussions’ regarding ‘possible transaction’ in relation to M1

The two companies will continue to work separately while regulators review the deal. TalkTalk, which has lost customers in recent years, was the UK’s fourth-biggest broadband provider with an 8% market share, according to a 2025 Ofcom report. BT, formerly the UK’s phone monopoly, was the largest with a 30% share.

UK State Secretary for digital Lisa Nandy will weigh wider public interest when reviewing the Competition and Markets Authority’s report on antitrust concerns. Critical infrastructure, including emergency services and hospital communications rely on TalkTalk’s services, Nandy’s department said in a statement.

Kirkby sought government assurances beforehand that a takeover of TalkTalk would not trigger an in-depth antitrust review, the Financial Times reported previously.

See also: 180 mil Singtel special discounted shares sold ahead of Nov 21 transfer

Over the last year, TalkTalk reported revenues of about £1.2 billion and was loss-making. The company has about 1.5 million retail customers and one million wholesale customers in the UK.

title: Sustainability tool launched to protect Asean access to US$780 bil US and EU fashion markets
article:
The Singapore Fashion Council (SFC) has launched the industry-first Sustainability Readiness Intelligence (SRI) tool on Oct 1 to help brands and manufacturers maintain and expand access to the global textiles and clothing export market.

In particular, the tool aims to help businesses protect their access to the US and EU markets, which are being reshaped by new regulations pertaining to ESG. According to sourcing platform SourceReady, the two markets are worth a combined US$780 ($999) billion in 2026, with the US importing around US$77.6 billion worth of apparel in 2025 and EU imports totalling around EUR180.5 ($258) billion in 2024,

For context, US states such as California are mandating Scope 3 disclosures for companies with more than US$1 billion in revenue from 2027, while brands operating in the EU will be subject to stricter supply chain due diligence obligations starting 2028.

Without robust data around reporting, traceability and documented sustainability practices, Asean manufacturers and brands face an immediate threat to their bottom line — losing preferred supplier status or getting locked out of future sourcing opportunities in the global market.

“Businesses across fashion and retail are navigating massive changes, including rising costs, global uncertainty, tariffs and rapid technological changes, even as consumers and markets expect more sustainable practices,” says Gan Siow Huang, Minister of State for Energy, Trade and Industry.

Gan, who was speaking at the SFC’s Be The Change Summit 2026, adds that companies that adapt early can become more “competitive” and “resilient” while unlocking new markets and business opportunities.

See also: How can Southeast Asia scale up energy transition investment?

The new tool will help Asean suppliers navigate the afore-mentioned evolving regulations. It uses an assessment framework to evaluate manufacturers’ readiness and sustainability maturity across five key dimensions: governance \and strategy, environment and operations, responsible supply chain, circularity and design, and market readiness.

In addition, the SRI offers customised recommendations for businesses according to their respective level of sustainability maturity, while considering broader industry trends and insights.

The assessment comprises more than 50 questions and produces a personalised business scorecard that helps to pinpoint key strengths and gaps against relevant market standards. It also generates a timed action roadmap, including applicable certifications and resources, for businesses.

Drawing directly from SFC’s new sectoral plan which was launched in tandem, the SRI serves as a practical guide that simplifies and brings together the most effective sustainability tools, frameworks and resources for fashion players in Singapore and Asean. The plan also complements the SRI by keeping businesses up-to-date on action they can take to enhance sustainability, notes the SFC.

“As global regulations raise the bar for compliance, the SRI tool helps to empower ASEAN businesses to meet stricter global ESG standards to maintain global export market access,” says SFC CEO Zhang Ting-Ting.

Zhang adds that the launch of the sectoral plan marks a “critical step” to future-proof the industry. “The implementation of SRI democratises opportunities for regional brands to capitalise on this sustainability-led momentum,” she remarks. “But more importantly, this will allow Asia to claim its seat at the global table and lead the fashion industry toward a more responsible model of growth.”

Both the sectoral plan and SRI are informed by an assessment report commissioned by SFC with research agency South Pole. Identifying sustainability gaps and opportunities across the Singapore and Asean fashion ecosystem, the report highlights how Singapore and its enterprises can leverage its strengths to drive regional collaboration, innovation, and scalable solutions.

“What Singapore lacks in fashion material production, we make up for in our role as a coordinator for design, logistics and sourcing,” says Zhang. “With many of the fashion brands’ Asian headquarters located here in Singapore, we are a vital nerve centre enabling us to amplify impact by facilitating stronger sustainable decisions and benchmarks across the whole value chain.”

title: Qualcomm licenses patents on Huawei’s LogicFolding chip tech — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 5): Qualcomm Inc has agreed to license patents underpinning Huawei Technologies Co’s novel LogicFolding chipmaking technique, a win for the Chinese company and its push to advance in overseas artificial intelligence (AI) markets.

The multiyear deal is part of a cross-licence agreement between the two chipmakers, spanning technologies related to 5G devices, AI services, near- and co-packaged optics and networks, a Huawei spokesperson said on Monday.

The agreement with Qualcomm helps validate the Shenzhen-based company’s chipmaking capabilities. Huawei sees its new architecture as a breakthrough that boosts semiconductor performance and helps it narrow the gap with industry leaders such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. That approach focuses on improving data transmission speeds to make up for China’s lack of access to ASML Holding NV’s extreme ultraviolet lithography machines, the gold standard for production of cutting-edge chips.

Huawei, which unveiled its LogicFolding approach just months ago, is one of a handful of companies seen as key to China’s ambitions to lead in AI and reduce reliance on foreign technology including Nvidia Corp accelerators. While hamstrung by US export curbs on advanced technologies, Huawei and its partners are exploring ways to design and produce the chips vital to data centres and AI development.

Before the US tightened restrictions on Huawei during President Donald Trump’s first term, the Chinese company sourced some smartphone chips from Qualcomm. Since Washington cut off Huawei’s access to advanced foreign chipmaking technology, Huawei has increasingly turned to domestically designed and manufactured semiconductors.

Huawei has also long been one of the world’s most prolific patent developers, particularly in wireless networking. In recent years, it’s stepped up efforts to earn revenue off its library of intellectual property, including licences to foreign companies.

See also: US stocks advance after cooler-than-expected employment data

The company did not disclose the value of the cross-licence agreement with Qualcomm. The deal is subject to US Federal Trade Commission review under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act, which applies to deals valued at more than US$133.9 million. Huawei expects the overall contract value of all its patent licensing agreements to exceed US$6.9 billion following the deal with Qualcomm, the spokesperson said.

title: UK job slump longer than during financial crisis, PMI says
article:
(Oct 5): Britain’s jobs market is stuck in its longest downturn since the early 2000s, according to a closely-watched survey, surpassing the decline during the financial crisis.

S&P Global’s UK purchasing managers’ index (PMI) said employers cut back on staff for a 24th consecutive month.

The figures will be a concern for Andy Burnham’s government ahead of the budget later this month with the intensifying energy shock and artificial intelligence (AI) threatening to dampen demand for workers. Employers have been shedding staff since the Labour government raised payroll taxes and the minimum wage shortly after returning to power in 2024.

There were some signs of the slump bottoming out, however, as job cuts in the services sector were the smallest in almost a year. Furthermore, Britain’s official unemployment rate remains much lower than during the period after the global financial crisis.

Britain’s labour market has been soft despite the wider economy smashing expectations during a resilient first half of the year. S&P’s survey suggested that the private sector is largely holding up against the energy shock for now, with demand boosted by stronger consumer spending and technology services amid a rush to harness AI.

See also: AMRO raises Asean+3 2027 growth forecast to 4.1% but expects higher inflation

The composite PMI eased to 52 in September from 52.5 the previous month, remaining above the 50 threshold separating growth from contraction. It was slightly better than the 51.7 reading in the flash estimate.

Still, the outlook has darkened since a resurgence in energy prices last month that has prompted traders to ramp up bets on the Bank of England raising interest rates several times to stop inflationary pressures spreading across the economy.

“Subdued demand conditions and rising inflationary pressures contributed to weaker business activity expectations for the year ahead,” said Tim Moore, economics director at S&P Global Market Intelligence. “Greater-than-expected business requirements seem to have helped to stem the jobs downturn in recent months.”

See also: BOJ’s deputy chief flags AI’s possible impact on neutral rate

The survey pointed to price pressures growing. Firms’ cost burdens and the prices they charge customers both rose at the quickest pace since June.

title: Radiant World misses salary payments for employees in September
article:
(Oct 5): Some employees of Radiant World say they have not received their September salaries, an apparent delay that offers a glimpse of disruptions inside the iron ore trader as its operations are transferred to the care of court-appointed managers.

The people, working in Singapore, China and Europe, said they had not been paid their wages on the usual schedule around the fourth week of the month, and that they were not aware of any colleagues having received anything as of Monday.

Several said there had been holdups in the past, with their monthly salaries ultimately paid as late as a few days into the new month. But they reported widespread concern among staff over the past week, given the multiple legal actions launched against the company.

A number of banks have cut Radiant World off since Bloomberg first reported in July on creditors’ concerns that the trader had been raising money using falsified documents. Some of the employees — all of whom asked not to be named as the issue is private — said that in recent months their salaries had been paid from a company account in Dubai.

It was not immediately clear what the cause of the delay was, or if the salaries would ultimately be paid. A spokesman for Radiant World did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

A spokesperson for KPMG, appointed as interim judicial manager last month, also did not respond to Bloomberg queries.

See also: ANZ to drop scandal-hit KPMG Australia as auditor after 57 years

Multiple lenders have accused Radiant World of providing falsified documents. Mizuho Bank Ltd, a creditor, began legal proceedings in August to remove the management of the merchant’s key operating company in Singapore, according to a court document seen by Bloomberg.

That was granted last month, when a Singapore court appointed KPMG to take charge. Restructuring executives from the firm have begun contacting current and former employees this week to arrange interviews, according to the people.

Mizuho said in a court filing that it had strong reasons to believe it was the victim of fraud perpetrated by Radiant World. The Singapore judge overseeing the case said in her ruling last week that the trader was, or was likely to become, unable to pay its debts.

See also: Singapore court strips control of Radiant World from founder

title: MAS may include insurance policies, digital payment tokens as Designated Investment assets for single family offices
article:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore is reviewing if assets classes such as insurance policies and digital payment tokens can be included as investments made by single family offices here, so that they can have more leeway to manage their portfolios and deploy capital here in Singapore.

"MAS is considering this feedback in its regular review of the tax policy framework, to keep pace with families’ evolving investment and wealth planning needs," says Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong, who wears another hat as chairman of Singapore's central bank.

The additions, if any, will be included in the updated Designated Investment list, which sets out the types of investments that can qualify for tax exemption under Singapore’s tax incentive schemes for funds.

Asset classes now in the list include shares, debt securities, funds, commodities, real estate and tokenised assets.

MAS will announce the updated Designated Investment list and implementation date in due course, says Gan, speaking at an event organised by the Wealth Management Institute on Oct 5.

In February, Manulife Singapore sold a US$300 million life insurance policy, breaking a US$250 million record set by HSBC Life in 2024.

See also: HSBC taps growing demand from HNW entrepreneurs with launch of Access in Singapore

In the prior 12 months, Manulife sold 25 individual policies each worth more than US$50 million.

"The transaction reflects the growing sophistication of high net worth planning needs, as families seek insurers with the financial strength, global perspective, and in-depth expertise to address multi-generational needs across different geographies," said Manulife Singapore then.

"Singapore's political and economic stability, coupled with its robust regulatory regime, continues to position the city-state as a key destination for HNW wealth management," Manulife added.

See also: Jefferies stung by soured bets at asset-management unit

Singapore as a wealth management hub has seen further growth.

According to Gan in his speech on Oct 5, in the past five years, private banking client assets here in Singapore grew by around 50%, with client assets up 15% between 2024 and 2025.

"This reflects the confidence that global and Asian families continue to place in Singapore as a wealth management hub and long-term partner," says Gan. "We must continue to deepen this confidence."

title: Nvidia’s valuations show AI rally isn’t a bubble, DBS says
article:
(Oct 5): Nvidia Corp’s price-to-earnings multiple and projected 70% earnings growth for next year demonstrate that artificial intelligence-driven technology stocks remain far from bubble territory, DBS Group chief investment officer Hou Wey Fook said.

Nvidia trades at 17 times its 12-month forward earnings, data compiled by Bloomberg showed, which Hou compared to Cisco System Inc’s 100 times valuation before the dot-com crash.

“If I describe the poster child of AI trading at mid-teens, how can it be a bubble?” he said in a Bloomberg TV interview, adding that there are still “tailwinds to this play on the semiconductor, this play on AI.”

Still, Hou advocates a “barbell” approach to “control the overall volatility of the portfolio” with AI, pairing technology stocks on the growth side with investment-grade fixed income for income stability, along with hedge funds and gold serving as risk diversifiers in the middle.

title: US, India officials signal trade deal talks at an impasse
article:
(Oct 5): Top officials in the US and India signalled that negotiations over a trade deal have reached an impasse that is making it difficult to clinch an agreement.

Indian Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said Monday that talks have “reached a plateau” beyond which a compromise would be difficult. That followed comments from United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on Friday that a trade deal was in its final stages but not "imminent".

The two sides agreed to an interim deal earlier this year and have been locked in negotiations ever since. Indian officials have sought assurances from the US that the country would have a favourable tariff rate over its peers and that it would not face additional penalties once the trade deal is signed.

Speaking at the Munich Security Conference on Monday, Sitharaman said trade negotiations have been difficult and rigorous, and “we would like to believe that both sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult”.

“Maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” she said.

The talks have been complicated by new US legislation giving US President Donald Trump the ability to impose tariffs of as much as 100% on the top buyers of Russian oil and gas. India, a major importer of Russian energy, has warned that such measures could hurt bilateral ties with the US and disrupt global energy markets.

See also: Wall Street’s US$10 bil India hospital bet sparks a fight over bills

US-India ties have come under strain in the past 18 months, with Trump imposing punitive tariffs on India for buying Russian oil before removing them. The US leader has repeatedly claimed he’d helped mediate a ceasefire to end a brief armed conflict between India and Pakistan in May 2025. New Delhi has consistently rejected Trump’s version of events.

Trump and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi held their first phone call since June last week, discussing trade and energy, as well as defence and critical minerals.

See also: RBI’s short dollar book surges past US$200 bil on forex plan

India’s External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar on Sunday warned that the US was becoming increasingly isolated in the new global order.

“Nobody would disagree with the fact that the landscape today is primarily marked by a radical repositioning of the United States,” he said at the Munich Security Conference. “A repositioning which is a posture of choice and where it has deliberately become a lonelier power.”

Rising competition between the US and China has also led to the "weaponisation of any leverage that any country has”, he said.

Indian Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal held what he described as “productive talks” with Greer in Milwaukee on the sidelines of the Group of 20 trade ministers’ meeting last week.

Greer said on Friday officials were working to iron out their disputes.

“I would characterise and say we are in the short strokes,” Greer said. The two sides have identified the “universe of items that are sticking points and we are working diligently toward them”, he said.

title: Denmark data breach exposes 8.8 mil people’s personal data
article:
(Oct 5): Denmark suffered a major data breach that gave unauthorised individuals access to names, addresses and personal identification numbers belonging to about 8.8 million people registered in the country’s central population database.

The breach occurred after unidentified individuals misused a private Danish company’s legitimate access to search the Central Person Register, known as CPR, the government said in a statement Monday.

The company has since been blocked from the system while police investigate the matter, with authorities saying it’s too early to determine who was behind the breach.

“This is a deeply serious incident,” Digitalisation Minister Christina Egelund said. She has ordered a comprehensive security review of the CPR system and urged Danes to be vigilant about suspicious calls and emails.

The CPR system is a cornerstone of Denmark’s highly digitised public sector. Every resident is assigned a unique 10-digit CPR number that is widely used to identify individuals when dealing with government agencies, banks and healthcare providers. While Denmark has a population of about six million, the register contains records on roughly 11 million people, including those who have died or moved abroad.

The administration first detected irregular activity on Oct 2 and determined over the weekend that unauthorised searches had taken place during September. People registered in the system for name and address protection were not exposed, it said.

See also: ECB seeks Schnabel successor in first move to post-Lagarde era

title: Copper gains as US jobs data offers relief on fed tightening
article:
(Oct 5): Copper rose for a second session after a US employment report eased pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates.

Futures climbed as much as 0.9% on the London Metal Exchange on Monday before trimming gains as the dollar strengthened on euro weakness. On Friday, copper had seen the biggest weekly loss since March, hit by data showing industrial weakness in China.

US data showed nonfarm payrolls rising just 29,000 last month, below all estimates by economists surveyed by Bloomberg. That led traders to pare bets that the Fed would hike rates this month, which would be negative for non-yielding assets like commodities.

Prices for the red metal are still consolidating near record levels after the threat of US tariffs saw traders ship hundreds of thousands of tonnes of metal into the country, potentially squeezing supply elsewhere. Meanwhile, demand is being bolstered by consumption by data centres and renewable energy.

Copper rose 0.5% to trade at US$14,331.50 a tonne on the LME by 3.33pm Singapore time. Zinc fell 0.3% and aluminium added 0.5%.

Singapore iron ore futures declined 0.2% to US$91.15 a tonne. Chinese traders are still away for the Golden Week holiday, which may be curbing market liquidity across metals.

See also: Glencore expects its commodity-trading profits to top US$5 bil this year

title: LNG trade through Hormuz extends rebound despite shipping risks
article:
(Oct 5): Shipments of liquefied natural gas through the Strait of Hormuz extended a rebound that began in September, as the region’s producers seek to restore supplies to energy-starved customers.

At least three LNG shipments have exited the key waterway since late last week, according to ship-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg and Kpler. While outbound traffic in September climbed to the highest level since the Iran conflict began in late February, flows remain more than 75% below pre-war levels.

The market is closely watching LNG shipments through Hormuz for signs of relief from a supply crunch that last month pushed prices in Europe and Asia to the highest since late 2022. A sustained recovery could help ease prices just before the Northern Hemisphere winter, when heating demand typically surges.

The increase in traffic comes as risks to shipping remain acute following a flurry of incidents in recent days. UK Maritime Trade Operations said it received a report of a tanker being hit by an unknown projectile within Hormuz on Oct 4.

title: Why the MEA–ASEAN corridor matters for sustainable growth
article:
The global economy is being reshaped by new patterns of trade, investment and capital flows. One of the most significant developments is the strengthening connection between the Middle East and Africa (MEA) and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

For QNB Group, ASEAN is an important strategic focus within our broader international growth ambitions. The region brings together fast-growing markets with expanding consumer demand, increasing manufacturing capacity and significant infrastructure requirements. As economic ties between Asia and MEA deepen, we see a clear role for QNB in connecting businesses and investors across the two regions and helping to facilitate the trade and investment flows between them.

ASEAN attracted a record US$243.9 billion ($311.67 billion) in foreign direct investments (FDIs) in 2025, an increase of 9.7%, outpacing FDI growth globally and across developing economies. The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) is already ASEAN’s seventh-largest trading partner, with two-way trade reaching US$130.7 billion, and the two regions are studying the establishment of a free trade agreement. The GCC has also set an ambition to increase trade with ASEAN to US$180 billion by 2032. Meanwhile, most tariffs on products traded within ASEAN have been eliminated under the ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement, supporting deeper regional integration.

These figures demonstrate the scale of the opportunity. However, I believe the next phase of growth between MEA and ASEAN will not be defined simply by higher trade volumes. It will depend on whether businesses can convert greater regional connectivity into practical commercial opportunities and whether financial institutions can provide the capital, infrastructure and local expertise needed to make that possible.

The MEA and ASEAN regions bring complementary strengths to this emerging corridor. ASEAN offers extensive manufacturing capabilities, large consumer markets and rapidly developing technology sectors. The Middle East provides significant pools of capital, expanding logistics infrastructure and access to markets across Africa and Europe.

However, ambition alone is not enough. Companies operating across this corridor must navigate different regulatory systems, currencies and market practices. They must decide where to establish operations, how to structure supply chains, where to hold liquidity and how to manage cross-border financial risks.

This is where international banking networks create real strategic value. Banks must do more than finance individual transactions. They need to understand a client’s broader commercial objectives and connect those objectives with the right markets, expertise and financial infrastructure.

At QNB Group, our role is to help clients translate regional ambitions into practical execution. This means working with them early in their decision-making process and providing continuity as they establish operations, manage liquidity, finance trade and mobilise capital for future growth.

Trade finance remains particularly important to the development of the MEA–ASEAN corridor. The Asian Development Bank estimates that the global trade finance gap stood at US$2.5 trillion in 2025, restricting the ability of many businesses to fulfil orders, expand supplier relationships or enter new markets.

Through our work with clients, we are already seeing how changing trade and investment patterns are translating into financing needs. In Indonesia, QNB supported a US$1 billion syndicated facility for one of the world’s largest pulp and paper companies, a US$350 million petrochemicals financing and a US$151.5 million facility for a Southeast Asian conglomerate. Corporate lending increased by 17% during the year, supported by syndicated and bilateral transactions.

ASEAN’s continued development will also require sustained investment in transport, logistics, digital infrastructure, energy and industrial capacity. These projects are capital-intensive, involve multiple stakeholders and often extend across several years.

Increasing the contribution from our international network is one of the cornerstones of QNB Group’s strategy for 2030. ASEAN’s role within this strategy reflects both the region’s growth potential and its increasing connectivity with our core markets across the GCC and wider MEA region.

Our Asian network spans Singapore, Hong Kong, India and Indonesia, supported by representative offices in mainland China and Vietnam. This presence, combined with our extensive network across the Middle East and Africa, enables us to connect clients with opportunities, capital and expertise across the corridor.

Our ambition is not simply to expand our geographic reach. It is to increase the value our network creates for clients by strengthening relationships, deepening our capabilities and connecting markets more effectively.

As trade and investment continue to evolve, the most successful businesses will be those that can operate confidently across regions while responding to local realities. I believe the MEA–ASEAN corridor will play an increasingly important role in this next phase of global growth and banks with the right network, expertise and strategic commitment will be essential to unlocking its full potential.

Khalid Ahmed Al-Sada, is the senior executive vice president – group corporate and institutional banking of QNB Group.

title: Wall Street’s US$10 bil India hospital bet sparks a fight over bills
article:
(Oct 5): Wall Street came to India chasing one of the world’s greatest hospital growth stories. It found something else too: a fight over who will pick up the bill.
